raw_response:
I am not going to do anything fancy. On my land, fancy talk does not fill the grain bag. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can really put out. I have 10.9 mu total, and with some people in the house working outside, I cannot manage all of it with labor-heavy crops. So I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is steady, and keep a smaller piece in cotton for cash. Wheat and maize are what I know best, and with the well I can protect them if the weather turns dry, but water costs money, so I will not overwater. For fertilizer, I would rather not let the crop go hungry, but I also cannot throw too much money into the field at once. I will put a solid base dressing, then watch the crop and add more if it looks weak. Cotton needs more hand work, so I will only keep it on a smaller area that the family can still handle.
